notes: Every target call enters two disposable bubblewrap user/mount namespace layers. The outer root maps only to the invoking host UID; inner root maps only to outer root. Inherited host mounts are locked read-only, checked by a denied bind-remount before every target call. Private PID/network namespaces and writable installation state are case-local; generated state is removed after each case while command evidence is retained.

Target environment keys BLACKBOX_SYSTEM_INSTALL_DIR and BLACKBOX_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR specify the expected compiled defaults; their reference-build defaults are /var/local/lib/flatpak and /usr/local/etc/flatpak. The namespace mounts private data at those paths, and CLI/C-client assertions still check the target's actual default location. These keys never become FLATPAK_SYSTEM_DIR or FLATPAK_CONFIG_DIR redirects. Set them under the target JSON environment object, not the host shell environment.

Readonly exposure includes only the suite directory, selected target executables, configured helpers and LD_LIBRARY_PATH directories. Uninstalled targets can explicitly add colon-separated absolute paths with BLACKBOX_TARGET_READONLY_PATHS in the target environment. No repository ancestor is inferred. Paths that cover private namespace roots or overlap protected installation/service content are rejected, including symlink aliases.

CLI deployment location checks use the public returned location, verify containment in the selected public installation base, locate the controlled bin/blackbox-probe payload there and execute it to distinguish A from B. They never construct a deployment path from a ref or commit, and never recursively search a general installation root for content.

Direct-root mutations may satisfy explicitly selected installation outcomes. These cases do not assert polkit authorization, non-root helper behavior, or multiple-user access. No requirement demanding those outcomes is mapped.
The named override case intentionally asserts the documented isolation contract; the reference target currently fails it, so that option receives no verified credit from that case.

behaviors.description: Install default, named and user copies, update each independently, then remove each independently.
behaviors.preconditions: Direct namespace-root access to private system stores; immutable A/B repositories.
behaviors.expected: Implicit install selects the actual default path; each update/removal leaves all other copies at their expected commits.

behaviors.description: Explicit system reinstall after removal, or-update, and reinstall of an older installed version.
behaviors.preconditions: Independent default A, named B, and user A deployments.
behaviors.expected: --system recreates the removed default copy; or-update and reinstall reach B while user A survives.

behaviors.description: Query installation-specific ref identity, actual location, metadata and typed lists.
behaviors.preconditions: A default/user app, B named app and explicit runtime copies.
behaviors.expected: Exact selected ref/commit/metadata and kind/architecture-filtered sets; public locations contain corresponding fixture content; emptied default list excludes user-only refs.

behaviors.description: Reject an unselected uninstall when the same full ref exists in multiple installations.
behaviors.preconditions: Default, named and user copies are installed.
behaviors.expected: Noninteractive ambiguity error identifies the app and every deployment retains its commit.

behaviors.description: Execute independently selected system, named and user applications.
behaviors.preconditions: Private session bus, nested sandbox capabilities, A/B fixture deployments.
behaviors.expected: Each selector executes its installation's version, including default system B versus user A.

mappings.rationale: Direct namespace-root install/update/uninstall outcomes are verified at actual system/named paths, including unchanged user commits and removal-query failure. No non-root authorization claim.

User install creates A under user path while named B and default A remain separate.
Default A changes to B while separately installed user A remains unchanged.
Named B downgrades to A while default B and user A are retained.
User A changes to B while default B and named A are retained.
Explicit A commit replaces named B even though origin still advertises B.
Default app becomes unqueryable while named A and user B survive.
Named app becomes unqueryable while user B survives.
User app becomes unqueryable while both competing system app copies and all explicitly installed runtimes remain.

mappings.rationale: Selected install operations are verified through exact commits and untouched user copy.

surface_assertions.rationale: A removed default app is recreated at A while named B and user A remain unchanged.
Repeat install changes default A to available B while user A survives.
Reinstall replaces explicitly downgraded default A with available B while user A survives.

mappings.rationale: All selected identity/metadata/type/architecture queries are exact; after emptying default, system list excludes the still-installed user app.
